problem.text: Suppose $P(x)$ is a quadratic polynomial with integer coefficients satisfying the identity $$P(P(x)) - P(x)^2 = x^2 + x + 2016$$ for all real $x$. Find $P(1)$

steps.title: Where to start: compare degrees
steps.body: The identity must hold for every $x$, so both sides must be the same polynomial. Write $P(x) = ax^2 + bx + c$ with $a \neq 0$. Then $P(P(x))$ means: put $P(x)$ in place of $x$, so the left side becomes $$aP(x)^2 + bP(x) + c - P(x)^2 = (a-1)P(x)^2 + bP(x) + c.$$

your_turn.prompt: If $a \neq 1$, what would the degree of the left side be? Why must $a = 1$?
your_turn.answer: Degree $4$: $(a-1)P(x)^2$ has leading term $(a-1)a^2x^4$, which is not zero, and $bP(x) + c$ has degree at most $2$, so nothing cancels it. The right side has degree $2$, so $a = 1$.

steps.title: Match the coefficients
steps.body: With $a = 1$ the $P(x)^2$ terms cancel, leaving $bP(x) + c = x^2 + x + 2016$ where $P(x) = x^2 + bx + c$. Expanding the left side gives $$bx^2 + b^2x + bc + c = x^2 + x + 2016.$$ Two polynomials are equal for all $x$ exactly when their matching coefficients are equal.

your_turn.prompt: Compare the $x^2$ coefficients and the $x$ coefficients. What is $b$?
your_turn.answer: The $x^2$ terms give $b = 1$, and the $x$ terms give $b^2 = 1$, which agrees. So $b = 1$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The constant terms give $bc + c = 2016$, and with $b = 1$ this is $2c = 2016$, so $c = 1008$. So $P(x) = x^2 + x + 1008$, which has integer coefficients as required, and $P(1) = 1 + 1 + 1008 = 1010$. The answer is **$1010$**.
